_help.about: [NOT WIRED YET — design §FX.5] Which of the game's biome templates (data/biomes/*.json, BiomeTemplates.KEYS) a land cell may become, given the RESOLVE 2017 biome its ecoregion belongs to. The ecoregion narrows the candidates; biome_pass's own climate and landform rules pick among them as they do today (the 'split' line says what should decide). Water, shore and landform templates are never chosen here: they come from the hydrology, geology and landform passes (see 'from_other_passes'). First guesses by Claude (chat), 18 Oct, from the RESOLVE biome definitions and the 52 templates' climate blocks; the designer owns them; tuned to what queue 105 reports.
_help.by_resolve_biome: Keyed by RESOLVE's BIOME_NUM (1–14; 'N/A' is RESOLVE's 'Rock and Ice'). templates: the candidates, the first one the fallback when no rule splits them. split: the rule of thumb for biome_pass, in plain words; the thresholds are Earth values and biome_pass applies HEIGHT_SCALE to heights as it does everywhere. gap: an Earth forest the 52 templates cannot yet show; a later data pass may add a template (§FX.5).
_help.from_other_passes: Templates that come from a pass, not from the ecoregion, and win over the ecoregion's list where their rule fires (as today).
_help.no_ecoregion: A land cell with no ecoregion within earth.json → ecoregions.nearest_fill_cells keeps today's climate rules over all 52 templates.

1.name: Tropical & Subtropical Moist Broadleaf Forests
1.split: CLOUD_FOREST above about 1,500 m Earth where the fog index is high; FLOODPLAIN_FOREST and SWAMP where the water passes say the ground floods; MANGROVE on tidal coasts (also from_other_passes); JUNGLE and TROPICAL_RAINFOREST as biome_pass tells them apart today (the disturbed, lighter, gap-rich forest against the closed canopy).

2.name: Tropical & Subtropical Dry Broadleaf Forests
2.split: THORN_SCRUB where annual precipitation is under about 600 mm or the soil is sharp; otherwise TROPICAL_DRY_FOREST.

3.name: Tropical & Subtropical Coniferous Forests
3.split: MONTANE_GRASSLAND above about 2,000 m Earth in Mexico (the realm is neotropic and the cell is north of 15°N); CLOUD_FOREST where fog is high; otherwise TROPICAL_DRY_FOREST.
3.gap: Tropical and subtropical conifer forest (Mexico's pine-oak, the Caribbean pine, the Sumatran and Luzon pines) has no template yet.

4.name: Temperate Broadleaf & Mixed Forests
4.split: TEMPERATE_RAINFOREST where annual precipitation is over about 1,400 mm and the coldest month stays above about −2 °C; MARITIME_FOREST within a cell of the coast on sand; FLOODPLAIN_FOREST and SWAMP where the water passes say so; otherwise TEMPERATE_DECIDUOUS.

5.name: Temperate Conifer Forests
5.split: TEMPERATE_RAINFOREST on the wet coasts (precipitation over about 1,400 mm); KRUMMHOLZ at the treeline band and ALPINE_MEADOW above it, as the altitude rules say today; TEMPERATE_DECIDUOUS where the mean annual temperature is above about 9 °C; otherwise TAIGA.
5.gap: Temperate conifer forest (the Rockies, the Sierra Nevada, the Alps' and Carpathians' conifer belt, inland Pacific Northwest, Hokkaido's firs) has no template yet; TAIGA stands in.

6.name: Boreal Forests/Taiga
6.split: BOG and FEN where the water passes say the ground is waterlogged (peat on the geology pass); KRUMMHOLZ at the treeline; otherwise TAIGA.

7.name: Tropical & Subtropical Grasslands, Savannas & Shrublands
7.split: THORN_SCRUB where annual precipitation is under about 500 mm; TROPICAL_DRY_FOREST where it is over about 1,200 mm; FRESHWATER_MARSH where the water passes say so; otherwise SAVANNA.

8.name: Temperate Grasslands, Savannas & Shrublands
8.split: In the nearctic: TALLGRASS_PRAIRIE where annual precipitation is over about 600 mm, SHORTGRASS_PRAIRIE below it. Elsewhere (the Eurasian steppes, the pampas, the veld): STEPPE. WET_MEADOW where the water passes say the ground is wet.

9.name: Flooded Grasslands & Savannas
9.split: SALT_MARSH on the coast or where the geology pass says salt; SWAMP where trees stand in the water (the warm, wet end); WET_MEADOW where the mean annual temperature is under about 10 °C; SAVANNA on the dry-season ground between the floods; otherwise FRESHWATER_MARSH.

10.name: Montane Grasslands & Shrublands
10.split: In the andes realm: PARAMO where annual precipitation is over about 900 mm (the wet north), PUNA where it is under (the dry centre and south). MONTANE_GRASSLAND in Mexico (neotropic north of 15°N) and on the African and Ethiopian highlands where the realm is afrotropic. ALPINE_TUNDRA where the mean annual temperature is under about 0 °C; otherwise ALPINE_MEADOW (the Tibetan, Alpine, Rocky Mountain meadows).

11.name: Tundra
11.split: ICE_SHEET where the mean annual temperature is under about −12 °C and the relief is the ice surface (Greenland's and Antarctica's interiors); GLACIER where the geology pass says ice on a slope; ALPINE_TUNDRA above the treeline on mountains outside the Arctic; BOG where the ground is waterlogged; otherwise TUNDRA.

12.name: Mediterranean Forests, Woodlands & Scrub
12.split: TEMPERATE_DECIDUOUS on the wet mountain side (precipitation over about 900 mm and the coldest month under about 5 °C); THORN_SCRUB on the driest ground (under about 300 mm); otherwise MEDITERRANEAN_SCRUB (the chaparral, matorral, fynbos, kwongan and maquis all read as this template; their plants differ by realm).

13.name: Deserts & Xeric Shrublands
13.split: HOT_DESERT where the mean annual temperature is over about 18 °C; COLD_DESERT below it; SAGEBRUSH in the nearctic where it is between about 5 and 12 °C (the Great Basin); THORN_SCRUB where annual precipitation is over about 250 mm; SALT_FLAT, OASIS, BADLANDS, CANYON and DUNES from their passes (from_other_passes).

14.name: Mangroves
14.split: MANGROVE on the tidal shore; SALT_MARSH where the mean annual temperature is under about 20 °C (mangroves' cold limit); LAGOON and ESTUARY from the water passes.

N/A.name: Rock and Ice
N/A.split: ICE_SHEET where the mean annual temperature is under about −12 °C; GLACIER on a slope under about −2 °C; ALPINE_TUNDRA on mountains; otherwise TUNDRA.
